reports.title: Copa Holdings Reports Third-Quarter Financial Results

guidance.heading: Outlook for 2026
section: While demand trends across the network continue to be strong, fuel prices have increased relative to the assumptions incorporated in the Company’s prior outlook. Based on current demand trends and fuel cost projections, the Company is updating its full-year 2026 outlook and now expects an operating margin in the range of 16% to 17% and a capacity increase in ASMs of approximately 14.5% compared to 2025.

Financial Outlook | 2026Guidance | 2025
Capacity – YOY ASM growth | ~14.5% | 7.8%
Operating Margin | 16-17% | 22.6%

Factored into this outlook are a load factor of approximately 87.5%, unit revenues (RASM) in the range of 12.3 to 12.4 cents, unit costs excluding fuel (Ex-Fuel CASM) of approximately 5.8 cents, and an all-in fuel price of approximately US$3.90 per gallon.

Preliminarily, for the full year 2027, the Company currently anticipates increasing its capacity measured in ASMs by approximately 8% to 9% compared to 2026, based on the current order book projection and consistent with Copa’s long-term growth plan. Copa’s unit cost outlook excluding fuel (Ex-Fuel CASM) is expected to be in the range of 5.7 to 5.8 cents.

desk.headline: Revenue up 32% to $1.2bn and EPS $4.29, both beat; 2026 margin outlook cut to 16–17% on fuel
results: Revenue rose 31.9% to $1.20bn on 16.3% more capacity and 13.5% higher unit revenue; planes were 88.7% full.
The fuel bill jumped 83.6% to $434.7m as the average price per gallon rose 61.5%, pulling the operating margin down to 18.6% from 23.2%.
Net profit edged up to $175.8m and EPS rose 2.2% to $4.29; unit cost excluding fuel was 5.7 cents, up 1.1%.
Cash and investments were about $1.6bn and net debt was 0.8x EBITDA; a Q4 dividend of $1.71 a share is payable on 15 Dec.
An October earthquake in Panama forced about 295 cancellations and is expected to cut Q4 operating profit by $12–14m.

guidance.summary: Copa cut its 2026 operating margin target to 16–17% because fuel is dearer than assumed, while keeping capacity growth at about 14.5%. It gave a first 2027 view of 8–9% more capacity.

points: Demand was described as strong in every region, with most of Q4 already sold and unit revenue for the rest of 2026 tracking above earlier assumptions.
Management said about 86% of the extra fuel cost was recovered through higher revenue, and expects fares to stay "pretty sticky" if fuel eases.
About 12 Boeing 737 MAX 8 deliveries are expected in 2027, weighted to Q4; Boeing's production limits are a delay risk, though no delays have been notified.
The Panama hub moves from six to eight connecting banks from March 2027, and Starlink Wi-Fi should be on the whole fleet by mid-2027.
No shares were bought back in the quarter; about $59m remains under the buyback programme.
